# Reusable Bottle Design Notes

Original short reference notes authored for 3di-men's test suite.

## Body, Shoulder, and Neck

A reusable bottle's body is the main cylindrical or near-cylindrical
volume that holds the contents. The shoulder is the curved transition
region that narrows the body down to the neck; it should be a smooth
curve rather than a sharp step, since a sharp step concentrates stress and
is harder to manufacture cleanly by blow molding or 3D printing. The neck
is the narrow cylindrical section the cap engages with.

## Cap Clearance

The cap must have a small clearance gap relative to the neck's outer
diameter, typically 0.2mm to 0.5mm, so it can be removed and replaced
without binding. A cap modeled at the exact same diameter as the neck is a
common mistake and will not fit in practice.

## Wall Thickness

A typical reusable bottle wall thickness is 1.5mm to 2.5mm. Thinner walls
risk collapsing under normal handling; much thicker walls waste material
and add unnecessary weight.
